topStory.headline: Academic Libraries Emerge as Campus A.I. Literacy Hubs
topStory.summary:
Academic libraries are evolving into what researchers call "A.I. sandboxes," neutral spaces where students and faculty can experiment with tools responsibly, according to Inside Higher Ed. At Bryn Mawr College, the library is using a platform called BoodleBox that gives centralized access to multiple A.I. tools while prioritizing privacy. At West Point, librarians developed a custom curriculum-mapping chatbot. Carnegie Mellon and the University of Pennsylvania offer hands-on A.I. literacy workshops.

Lauren Dodd at Bryn Mawr stated that "A.I. literacy is just a new dimension of information literacy." The skills librarians have been teaching — evaluating sources, understanding bias, thinking critically about information — apply directly to working with A.I. systems.

BoodleBox, one platform being used, serves over 800,000 users across more than 1,300 campuses. Libraries are positioned as neutral spaces not tied to any single department or discipline, serving everyone from first-year students to doctoral researchers with a tradition of teaching information skills.

stories.headline: San Diego Colleges Host InnovAItion Day
stories.summary: The San Diego Community College District is hosting InnovAItion Day on March 20, bringing together faculty, staff, and students to explore responsible A.I. use in education, according to SD City Times. The event features student-led panels and discussions about A.I.'s role in learning.

stories.headline: Survey: 70% of Students Now Use A.I. Weekly for Education
stories.summary: A Jobs for the Future survey finds student A.I. use for education increased from 59% in 2024 to 70% in 2026, according to Inside Higher Ed. However, 48% seek A.I. guidance from social media versus 23% from educational institutions, indicating students prefer informal learning channels.

stories.headline: EU A.I. Act Enters Full Effect for Universities in August
stories.summary: The EU AI Act classifies A.I.-assisted admissions systems and student performance analytics as "high-risk," requiring European universities to demonstrate compliance by August 2026 or face penalties, according to The Education Magazine. The regulation represents the most comprehensive A.I. governance framework affecting higher education globally.
